I hereby approve this thesis to be applied for examination. 指導教授簽章： Advisor's Signature . 共同指導教授簽章（如有）： Co-advisor’s Signature (if any) . 日期： Date(yyyy/mm/dd) . / / iii ABSTRACT With the vast positive trend of e -commerce sales, the efficiency of warehouse operations needs to keep pace.

Therefore, a part -to-picker warehouse named Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System Warehouse (RMFS) was explicitly designed e -commerce warehouse. This warehouse system can reduce the number of human operators and use robots, or in RMFS , called Automated Guided Vehicle s ( AGV), to carry the pods. There are several ways to increase the efficiency of the warehouse.

This research will focus on the decision problem, SKU to the Pod, or product assignment policy. This research has three scenarios: SKU to Pod using Random—baseline, Mixed Class, and Mixed Class Affinity policy. ABC classification and association rule using Weighted Support Count is applied to desig n the second and third scenarios. Then, using a simulation approach, those three scenarios are compared to find the best policy to increase warehouse efficiency.

It is indicated by looking at each policy's number of pods transported. The smaller the number of pods, the higher pile -on the SKU to pod policy achieves. As a result, the last scenario yields the best pile -on with an average number of pods transported of 6.59 pods per order .

Meanwhile, the first and second scenarios' results are 7.06 and 6.90, respectively. From that numbers, it can be concluded that the pile-on of the last scenario is 7% and 5% higher than the other two scenarios, even though only 8% of SKUs form the association's rule . This result is verified by using one-way ANOVA. According to research, 52% of consumers avoid shopping in person and also avoid crowded areas. Furthermore, 36% avoid shopping in person until they get a coronavirus vaccine (Bhatti et al., 2020).

Therefore, online shopping is one of the most popular online activities worldwide. In 2020, retail e-commerce sales worldwide reached US$4.28 trillion, and e-retail revenue is projected to grow to US$6 .4 trillion by 2024, as depicted in Figure 1.1 (Chevalier, 2021).

Figure 1.1 E-commerce Sales Worldwide With the growth of e-commerce sales, the efficiency of warehouse operations also needs to keep pace. The Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) warehouse was designed specifically for e-commerce. This warehouse system can reduce the number of human operators and use robots or RMFS, usually called AGV (Automated Guided Vehicles), to carry the shelves, called pods, to the picking stations instead (Merschformann et al., 2019).

This type of warehouse can also be categorized as a partto-picker warehouse because the parts, or p roducts, are moved to the picking stations then the operator collects the products (Murray, 2019). In the entire warehouse, order 0 1000 2000 3000 4000 5000 6000 7000 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 Billion US Dollar Year E-commerceSales Worldwide 2 picking activity is usually the most time -consuming compared t o others (Frazelle, 2016).

Therefore, increasing the efficiency of order picking also increases warehouse efficiency. There are several ways to increase the efficiency of the warehouse. It is divided into three levels of decision problems. These are the strategic, tactical, and operational levels (Merschformann et al., 2019) .

Product assigning is a strategic decision that affects order-picking efficiency (Li et al., 2020) . Therefore, des igning a good policy for product assignment is vital to achieving order-picking efficiency(Silva et al., 2022). Product assigning itself has three decision problems. Those are products (SKU) to pod, pods to zones, and product dispersion over multiple pods (Mirzaei et al., 2022) .

This research will focus on the first decision problem, products to pod or product assignment policy. There are three popular product assignment policies which are random, dedicated, and class-based storage assignment policies (Gu et al., 2007).

The random assignment policy is clear and straightforward; the SKU randomly assigns the Pod (Mirzaei et al., 2022). On the other hand, a dedicated assignment policy is when each storage location is only used for one particular product. This policy will obtain optimal picking travel distance (Muppani & Adil, 2008) . Chan and Chan (2011) had a simulation between random and dedicated assignment policies. The result showed that these policies help to maximize the utilization of storage space and the system throughput , respectively.

Using a random instead of dedicated policy might require a smaller warehouse but more effort to track inventor y accuratel y (Gu et al., 2007) . Class -based storage assignment policy assigns the products after it grouped into classes based on the order frequency (Silva et al., 2022) .

This policy with two or three classes can achieve the most advantages (Yuan et al., 2018) . The two advantages are significant cost savings and space sharing (Mirzaei et al., 2021; Muppani & Adil, 2008).

Other than those three popular policies, there is another policy for product assignment called the cluster-based storage assignment policy. This policy clusters correlated items and then assign s the products into the Pod based on the cluster to minimize the inventory and material handling cost (Kim, 1993). RMFS warehouses 3 can get advantages from clustering the frequent order together products on the same Pod (Mirzaei et al., 2021). Applying this policy saves order-picking efforts and reduces retrieval time significantly (Frazelle & Sharp, 1989; Mirzaei et al., 2021). Almost all cluster -based policy researches prove that storage assignment using cluster-based policy is better than other policies based on their objectives.

However, none of them are trying to find the best product mixture that could be applied in any other similar cases. The product mixture is the optimal combination of the product classes on pods that minimize the number of pods transported.

The fewer pods that need to be transported, which may dec rease the number of AGVs needed, the higher pile-on is (Merschformann et al., 2019) . Pile -on is when the pods offer most units necessary to fulfill the orders(Merschformann et al., 2019).

An appropriate product classification also increases order-picking efficiency (Chan & Chan, 2011) . Generally, ABC classification is the most common ly used in warehouse product classification based on order frequency.

However, this classification usually solves the second de cision problem of product assignment: Pod to zones. Besides, they all use the one-class-one-pod rule, and none try to find the best product class mixture (Products to Pod) for each Pod. Therefore, this research aims to maximize pile-on by finding the best product mixture. 1.2 Objective Based on the background previously described, the objectives of this research can be described as follows: 1. To determine the optimal product mixture percentage within the warehouse by analyzing the various factors influencing warehouse space utilization. 2. To establish the best policy for the SKU to pod decision problem by employing a simulation-based approach. This objective aims to determine the most suitable and effective strategy for allocating products to specific storage po ds, considering various constraints such as demand patterns, inventory levels, and available space. Furthermore, the simulation approach will enable us to analyze the performance of different strategies and determine the one that offers the best results. 4 1.3 Scope and Limitation The following limitations of the research must be acknowledged: 3.

text: 6 CHAPTER 2 LITERATURE REVIEW 2.1 Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) As e -commerce has become more prevalent, researchers seek more efficient methods of managing warehouses and improving picking operations to reduce costs and inefficiencies (Galliussi, 2022) . A robotic mobile fulfillment system (RMFS) warehouse is a solution for e -commerce sales growth because it fits many SKUs and demands multiple small-quantity orders (Azadeh et al., 2019).

section: 5. Chapter 5: Conclusion and Future Work. This chapter summarizes the study's
text: In addition, this type of warehouse is introduced as a solution for automated storage/retrieval system (AS/RS) warehouse problems which are th e rigidity of changing inventory locations, the high cost of setup, and manual re-slotting (Enright & Wurman, 2011; Wurman et al., 2008). The solution offered by RMFS is robots that carry pods on the conventional warehouse called shelves, with items on the pods (Enright & Wurman, 2011) . The robots carry one Pod for each robot from storage locations to replenishment or picking stations for later the pods being filled or picked by the workers (Kim et al., 2020).

text: Each picking station receives a customer order when it arrives. Then pods containing items in the order are transported to the station by robots. The operators remain at their stations because all items are carried by robots (Enright & Wurman, 2011). The RMFS layout is commonly arranged with storage zones of inventory pods, replenishment stations, and picking stations. The illustration can be seen in Figure 2.1.

section: 5. Chapter 5: Conclusion and Future Work. This chapter summarizes the study's
text: There are several benefits of the RMFS warehouse. In 2016, it was found t hat RMFS's throughput is higher than AS/RS depending on the number of AGVs and SKUs (Beuters et al., 2016) . The throughput increases when the inventory is dispersed into multiple pods, the warehouse has an optimal number of stations, and the pods are replenished before empty Tessensohn et al. (2020). The other benefit is that the system can quickly adapt to new replenishment policies, and even if a robot breaks down, it will not affect productivity significantly (Enright & Wurman, 2011).

section: 5. Chapter 5: Conclusion and Future Work. This chapter summarizes the study's
text: The Jaccard Index, developed by Swis s mathematician Paul Jaccard, is a well -known measure of similarity between sets that considers their similarities and differences. This method has been widely used in various fields, including information retrieval and data mining, to quantify the similar ity between different sets of items. The study also employs the Jaccard Index to measure the association between goods in a storage assignment study. On the other hand, the Weighted Support Count (WSC), which represents the relationship between any pair of goods, incorporates the concepts of support and lift developed by Ming-Huang Chiang et al. (2014) . The study results show that the Weighted Support Count outperforms the Jaccard Index in terms o f accuracy and effectiveness, as Yang (2022) demonstrated. This comparative study provides valuable insights into selecting the most appropriate method for a specific data analysis problem and contributes to the ongoing research in association rule mining. 10 CHAPTER 3 METHODOLOGY The steps outlined in this chapter serve as a comprehensive guide for the research process to ensure that it aligns with the stated objectives.

text: 3.3.1 Random Assignment Scenario In the random scenario of the SKU-to-Pod assignment process, the SKUs are assigned to Pods randomly, taking into account the data order and inventory analysis conducted in the preceding step. However, it should be noted that this scenario operates within a set of guidelines, specifically that each SKU is dispersed across several Pods. This random scenario acts as a baseline for comparison with the other scenarios, serving as a starting point for further analysis. The results of the random scenario provide a foundation for determining the impact of different approaches to the SKUto-Pod assignment process 14 3.3.2 Mixed-Class Assignment Scenario The mixed-class assignment scenario requires the completion of three key steps. Firstly, the product mixture percentag e must be calculated using the principles of Independent Event probability as described in Equations (2) and (3). As per Shafer (1996), independent events do not depend on one another for their occurrence. Therefore, this calculation determines the appropriate number of Pods for each class combination, as the orders between classes are not interdependent. Thus, the independent event probability is used to establish the probability of each product mixture.

The results of these three steps provide a comprehensive analysis of the mixed - class assignment scenario, allowing for a th orough evaluation of the impact of prioritizing high-frequency SKUs on the efficiency of the Pod system. text: 3.4 Simulation In this study, the simulation of the three SKU-to-Pod assignment scenarios will be conducted using the NetLogo software. The simulation will generate the number of pods visited for each scenario to evaluate the efficiency of the scenarios. This evaluation will be based on the number of pods visited and comparing them with the other two scenarios. The objective is to determine which scenario produces the highest pile and hence, the most efficient storage allocation of the SKUs in the Pod system.

text: 3.4.1 Simulation Layout The design of the warehouse simulation in NetLogo is depicted in Figure 3.4. The simulation consists of three distinct sections: the picking station, the storage area, and the replenishment station.

text: First, the picker awaits the arrival of AGVs carrying pods at the picking station . Next, the storage area is where the pods are stored, ready to be carried by AGVs. Finally, the replenishment station is where empty pods are refilled, 17 ensuring that the storage area remains fully stocked. The following are the key elements found in the storage area of the warehouse in NetLogo: 1. Pod: A container where items are stored. 2. Selected Pod: A Pod that has been chosen and matches the items with the assigned orders. 3. AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle): A robot responsible for transporting pods to the picking and replenishment station. 4. Aisle: The designated path for AGV to move and access pods in the storage area. 5. Empty Storage Location: An available space in the storage area where pods can be stored.
